analysis.investment_thesis: BEML fails the Magic Formula on both dimensions: earnings yield is a paltry ~3.4% (Operating Income INR 506 Cr ÷ EV ~INR 15,075 Cr) and ROCE of 15.6% is mediocre for a capital-heavy industrial. The stated operating margin of -1.63% suggests true EBIT (post-D&A) is likely negative, making the formula mathematically incoherent.
key_strengths: Government-backed order book across defense, metro, and mining — provides revenue visibility
Operating Income CAGR of 14.6% over 9 years shows improving operational leverage
Low D/E of 0.24 and largely PSU-linked customer base limits credit risk
key_risks: Reported operating margin of -1.63% implies EBIT is likely negative after D&A — Magic Formula breaks down entirely
Revenue CAGR of only 3.4% over 9 years shows near-stagnant top-line growth despite capital deployed
FCF highly volatile (INR -8 Cr in FY2025, INR -351 Cr in FY2021) and capex surging to INR 193 Cr signals capital trap
red_flags: Negative operating margin (-1.63%) despite headline 'Operating Income' appearing positive — definitional mismatch signals poor EBIT quality
Earnings yield of ~3.4% is less than half the 6% minimum threshold for the Magic Formula
Borrowings swung from INR 71 Cr to INR 666 Cr in a single year while cash sits at only INR 4 Cr
analysis.detailed_analysis:
BEML is a PSU conglomerate serving defense, metro rail, and mining — sectors with long gestation cycles and government procurement risk. The Magic Formula requires both a high earnings yield AND high return on capital; BEML delivers neither. At EV ~INR 15,075 Cr against EBIT of, at best, INR 506 Cr, the earnings yield is ~3.4%, and the true post-D&A EBIT appears negative given the -1.63% operating margin. ROCE of 15.6% is passable but not the 25%+ Greenblatt looks for.

Free cash flow converted to strongly negative in FY2025 (INR -8 Cr) as capex spiked to INR 193 Cr (vs. INR 101 Cr prior year) — CWIP jumped from INR 37 Cr to INR 171 Cr — absorbing cash without earnings to show for it. Net profit of INR 293 Cr against a P/E of 59.3x means you are paying a steep premium for a low-ROIC industrial. Until the company demonstrates sustained positive EBIT margins and earnings yields north of 8%, this is a pass.
